findings.claim: In September 2025 Amazon agreed to pay $2.5 billion ($1 billion civil penalty, $1.5 billion in refunds) to settle FTC charges over Prime enrolment and cancellation, without admitting wrongdoing. By September 2026 it had refunded over $845 million; a court-approved revision raised the refund cap to $200, with all payments due by April 2027.

The FTC, joined by state attorneys general, alleges in a 2023 suit (W.D. Wash. 2:23-cv-01495) that Amazon unlawfully maintains an online retail monopoly. The case is pending; in October 2026 the judge refused Amazon's request to delay the trial set for 29 March 2027.

On 31 August 2026 the FTC and 22 states sued Amazon, alleging that since 2019 it secretly added a surcharge to its search-ad auctions while presenting them as second-price auctions, overcharging over a million sellers. These are allegations in a pending case; no executive is named as a defendant.

California's attorney general sued Amazon in September 2022, alleging that its pricing policies kept prices high across online retail. In April 2026 the court denied Amazon summary judgment on a key crossclaim; the trial, first set for 19 January 2027, was moved to 22 March.

Italy's competition authority fined Amazon €1.13 billion in 2021 for abusing its dominance in e-commerce logistics. After a September 2025 court ruling, the authority cut the fine to €752.4 million in January 2026; Amazon said it would appeal and the regulator was also reported to appeal.

In March 2026 Luxembourg's appeal court annulled the €746 million GDPR fine imposed in 2021, for procedural failings, while confirming that Amazon's ad targeting lacked a valid legal basis and breached transparency rules. The case went back to the regulator, which may impose a new penalty.

In December 2023 the EU Court of Justice dismissed the European Commission's appeal, leaving annulled its 2017 decision that Luxembourg's tax treatment of two Amazon subsidiaries was illegal state aid. Amazon won this matter.

In January 2026 Amazon agreed to settle a class action alleging it failed to refund or re-charged customers for returned items: $309.5 million on top of more than $600 million paid or about to be paid, plus practice changes. The court gave preliminary approval in August 2026; final hearing is set for March 2027.

In December 2024 Amazon settled OSHA's ergonomics cases from inspections of 10 warehouses since 2022, paying $145,000 and agreeing to corporate-level ergonomic risk controls across its US facilities for two years.

Bezos owns The Washington Post. In February 2025 he announced that its opinion section would write daily in defence of personal liberties and free markets, leaving opposing views to other outlets; the opinion editor declined to stay.

Amazon's 2025 sustainability data, released July 2026, show absolute emissions up 16% on 2024, with Scope 3 (construction, products, third-party freight) up 20%, driven mainly by data-centre expansion. Its net-zero target is 2040.
The Bezos Day 1 Families Fund gave $102.5 million in homelessness grants to 32 nonprofits in December 2025, bringing its grants since 2018 to more than $850 million.
By April 2026 the Bezos Earth Fund had deployed about $2.4 billion of the $10 billion Bezos committed in 2020 for climate and nature, leaving about $7 billion to be disbursed by 2030.

ecology.reason: Mass retail, logistics and data centres. Amazon's own figures show absolute emissions up 16% in 2025, driven mainly by data-centre electricity and construction, products and third-party freight; its net-zero target is 2040.

politics.reason: Owns The Washington Post, and in 2025 personally set its opinion section to defend personal liberties and free markets. Amazon's lobbying not assessed here.

social.reason: Amazon paid $2.5 billion in 2025 to settle FTC charges that it enrolled customers in Prime without clear consent and made cancelling hard, without admitting wrongdoing. It also settled a class action over unpaid return refunds in 2026 and OSHA ergonomics cases at its warehouses in 2024.

legal.reason: Company settlement above $1 billion (FTC Prime case, 2025); no personal case. Italy's 2021 abuse-of-dominance fine was cut to €752.4 million in 2026 and is under appeal. Luxembourg's €746 million GDPR fine was annulled in 2026 on procedure, with the breaches confirmed. The EU lost its state-aid case against Amazon in 2023.

unresolved.reason: The FTC's antitrust case against Amazon, joined by states, is due for trial on 29 March 2027. The FTC and 22 states also sued in August 2026 over alleged hidden ad-auction surcharges, and California's price case is set for trial in 2027. All are company-level; none names Bezos.

proposal.counterweights: The Bezos Day 1 Families Fund has given more than $850 million in homelessness grants since 2018. The Bezos Earth Fund had deployed about $2.4 billion of a $10 billion climate commitment by 2026.
proposal.rationale: No value changes. All matters are company-level and none names Bezos, so legal and unresolved stay 2 (R5, R6). Ecology and politics move from estimate to documented at the same level. 'Packaging' in the current ecology reason was not re-sourced and is dropped. The existing source key 'amazon' now resolves to the FTC's 2026 ad-surcharge case page, not the monopolization case, so it was not reused; f2 cites the monopolization case page instead. Earth Fund 'deployed' may mean awarded rather than paid.
